props.title: American Boy: A Profile of Steven Prince

sections.content: American Boy: A Profile of Steven Prince (1978) is Martin Scorsese's raw, intimate documentary that captures former Neil Diamond road manager and Taxi Driver (1976) gun consultant Steven Prince in a cocaine-fueled story session. Prince's wild tales - particularly his adrenaline shot revival of an overdosed woman - directly inspired Quentin Tarantino's overdose scene in Pulp Fiction (1994). The documentary showcases Scorsese's ability to draw out compelling narratives from real characters, similar to his approach in Italianamerican (1974) with his parents.

sections.content: What makes American Boy particularly fascinating is how it captures a specific moment in late 1970s counter-culture, when the lines between Hollywood's mainstream and its fringes were blurring. Prince's stories about drug dealing, violence, and survival echo through later films like Goodfellas (1990) and True Romance (1993). His casual way of relating shocking events became a template for the kind of storytelling that would define indie cinema of the 1990s.

The documentary's influence extends beyond just Tarantino. Its raw interview style and focus on a magnetic but troubled personality influenced later works like Crumb (1994) and The Devil and Daniel Johnston (2005). The way Scorsese lets Prince command the room, spinning increasingly dark tales while the camera stays fixed on his animated face, created a template for character-driven documentaries. movies.title: Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker's Apocalypse
movies.slug: Documentary chronicling the troubled production of Apocalypse Now

sections.content: Scorsese's approach in American Boy demonstrates the power of letting subjects tell their own stories without interference. This influenced later documentary filmmakers like Errol Morris, whose Fast, Cheap & Out of Control (1997) similarly lets eccentric personalities drive the narrative. The film's intimate setting - mostly shot in a single room - creates an intensity that later documentaries like The Kid Stays in the Picture (2002) and Tyson (2008) would emulate.
